format: html

## Background

You are working with the same 150 stone artifacts as Assignment 1 (see
`artifacts.csv`: `artifact_id`, `site`, `raw_material`, `length_mm`,
`width_mm`, `thickness_mm`).

**How this assignment is graded.** Your figure is checked by saving it under an
*exact object name* (given below). The grader looks at the plot object itself:
which kind of marks it draws, which columns are mapped to which aesthetics, and
which labels it carries. Leave the chunk labels (the name after `r` in each
` ```{r name} ` line) as they are, because feedback points you to the chunk to
revisit. Use `ggplot2`.

```{r load-data}
library(ggplot2)
artifacts <- read.csv("artifacts.csv")
```

## Task 1: Length against width, by raw material

Make a scatter plot of the artifacts with:

- `length_mm` on the **x** axis and `width_mm` on the **y** axis,
- one point per artifact,
- the points **coloured by `raw_material`**,
- axis labels that say what is measured and the unit (for example
  "Length (mm)", not the column name),
- a plot **title**.

Save the plot as **`length_width_plot`**. Assign it with `<-`; you do not need to
print it or save it to a file, but printing it is a good way to check your work.

```{r scatter-plot}
length_width_plot <- ggplot(artifacts, aes(length_mm, width_mm, colour = raw_material)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(x = "Length (mm)", y = "Width (mm)")
```
